draft.title: Precise academic vocabulary
card: Academic writing about texts uses exact technical words. A vague word such as thing, good or shows tells the reader very little.
Juxtaposition
placing two different or opposite things side by side so the contrast stands out.
Characterisation
the ways a writer builds a character, such as through actions, speech and description.
Imagery
language that creates a picture or sense in the reader's mind, such as a description of a storm.
draft.remember: Name the exact technique instead of using a vague word.

a.q: Which phrase is the most precise way to complete this sentence? "The writer uses ___ to show that Tom is brave."
opts: a good thing, in his actions
a.why: Characterisation is the exact term for how a writer builds a character, and actions are one way of doing it. The other options use vague words such as thing, words and style, which name no technique.
a.clue: Which option names a technique rather than a vague word?

b.q: A student writes that a poem has a good thing in it, where a rich house sits next to a crumbling shack. Which word should replace "good thing"?
b.why: Placing a rich house beside a crumbling shack puts two opposites side by side, which is juxtaposition. Imagery is the tempting choice, but it names picture-making language, not a contrast between two things.
b.clue: Two opposite things are placed next to each other.
